Kbd

A keyboard key or shortcut named in text, such as Ctrl + K.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • To name the shortcut for an action that the view also offers as a control: beside a button, in a sentence of help, or in a list of shortcuts.
  • To name a key the reader presses in a terminal or a form, such as Enter or Esc.

When not to use it

  • As the only way to learn or reach an action. Every shortcut belongs to a button, a link or a menu item the reader can see and press.
  • For a command, a path or other text the reader types out. Use a code element.
  • For something the reader presses on screen. Use a button.
  • For a status or a count. Use a badge or plain text.

Variants

key
One key: a kbd element with the class gw-kbd.
combination gw-kbd__combo
Keys pressed together: an outer kbd with gw-kbd__combo holding one gw-kbd per key, with a plus sign and spaces written as text between them.

Sizes

default
12px mono text in a 1px border, about 19px tall. It fits a line of body text, a list row and a small button's row without adding height.

Accessibility

  • Use the kbd element. A screen reader reads the key's text in place, so write the key as a word or a character it can say: Ctrl, Shift, Enter, Esc, Up arrow, K. Do not use a symbol alone for a modifier, because it is read differently by each screen reader or not at all.
  • A combination is an outer kbd with gw-kbd__combo holding one kbd with gw-kbd per key, joined by a plus sign as text with a space each side: Ctrl + K. A screen reader then reads Ctrl plus K. Never draw the plus with a stylesheet or an icon.
  • Keys pressed one after the other are separate keys joined by the word then: G then R.
  • Name the platform's own key. Where the app knows the reader is on a Mac it writes Cmd in place of Ctrl; it does not show both.
  • A shortcut is never the only way to an action. Show it next to the control that does the same thing, or in a list the reader can open from a visible control.
  • A key is text. It is not focusable and takes no press, and it has no hover or pressed state.
  • The app wires the shortcut itself. For a button, set aria-keyshortcuts to the same keys, such as aria-keyshortcuts="Control+K", so assistive technology can report it.
